\sum_{\alpha=1}^2\mathsf g^{AB}\partial_A N_\alpha\cdot\partial_B N_\alpha
+S_{\mathrm{GHY},8},
\tag{U.44u.1}
$$
where $\kappa>0$, the inner product is Euclidean, and $\Lambda_8$ has units of inverse length squared. The original Dirichlet gravitational boundary term on $\partial B\times S^4$ is retained, with the outward normal and its standard nonnull sign. The reference construction uses no measured scalar or cosmological response. The use of spherical $\sigma$ winding as a compactification mechanism has a six-dimensional precedent (Lee and Papazoglou 2004).

Trace reversal and variation tangent to the unit spheres give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}(\mathsf g)
&=\frac{\Lambda_8}{3}\,\mathsf g_{AB}
+\frac{\kappa}{M_8^6}\sum_{\alpha=1}^2
\partial_A N_\alpha\cdot\partial_B N_\alpha,\\
0&=\Box_{\mathsf g}N_\alpha+
(\mathsf g^{AB}\partial_A N_\alpha\cdot\partial_B N_\alpha)N_\alpha .
\end{aligned}
\tag{U.44u.2}
$$
On $\mathsf g=g(x)\oplus R^2\gamma(y)$ take $N_1(y)=y$, the unit-sphere coordinate map in its declared orientation, and let $N_2$ depend only on $x$. The identity satisfies the sphere equation since $\Delta_\gamma y=-4y$ and its squared gradient in $\gamma$ is four. The first field's pullback metric is exactly $\gamma$ and the second contributes only to the external components. For a flat $g$ and constant $N_2$, the external equation requires $\Lambda_8=0$. The internal equation then reads $3\gamma=(\kappa/M_8^6)\gamma$. This fixes the common stiffness. The radius $R$ cancels from this comparison and may be fixed by product Dirichlet data. The reference admits every positive constant radius, giving a homogeneous radius modulus.

For arbitrary $g(x)$ and $N_2(x)$, the internal and mixed equations continue to hold at these values and fixed $R$. The remaining equations are exactly
$$
\operatorname{Ric}_{\mu\nu}(g)=3\,\partial_\mu N_2\cdot\partial_\nu N_2,\qquad
\Box_g N_2+(\partial_\mu N_2\cdot\partial^\mu N_2)N_2=0 .
\tag{U.44u.3}
$$
Thus any four-dimensional solution with the stated maps and boundary data solves all eight-dimensional bulk equations, including the omitted metric components. The second target admits its unit equatorial $S^2$ as a totally geodesic submanifold. In the extrinsic sphere equation, setting the other two coordinates identically zero preserves their equations and leaves the full first three equations. This is an exact consistent classical restriction, including for two independent tangential variations.

*Physical Hopf map and normalization.* Choose an $h$-orthonormal ordered frame of $\mathcal S_{-4}$ in Definition U.44b. In that frame write its unit vector as $(z_1,z_2)$, and use the physical target map
$$
N_2([z])=
\bigl(2\operatorname{Re}(\overline z_1 z_2),\
2\operatorname{Im}(\overline z_1 z_2),\
|z_1|^2-|z_2|^2,0,0\bigr) .
\tag{U.44u.4}
$$
The coordinates are the three Pauli expectations of the rank-one state in the marked frame. They have Euclidean norm one and descend through the common Hopf phase. For a horizontal variation at $(1,0)$, the derivative is $(2\operatorname{Re}\delta z_2,2\operatorname{Im}\delta z_2,0,0,0)$. Unitary covariance of the Bloch map gives the same squared-norm factor four everywhere, and polarization gives the metric identity $N_2^*g_{S^4}=4g_{FS}$. A change of the initial frame rotates the three physical axes and preserves their metric. The map identifies the retained ray with its measured direction, rather than rescaling the geodesic command. On the nominated one-field geodesic $[z]=[\cos d:\sin d]$ its image is $(\sin 2d,0,\cos 2d,0,0)$, with the original projective coordinate $d$.

Put $V_4=R^4\operatorname{Vol}(S^4,\gamma)$ and $\bar M^2=M_8^6V_4$. At the selected stiffness the internal gravitational density $M_8^6(12/R^2)/2$ cancels exactly the winding gradient density $\kappa(4/R^2)/2$. The induced outer extrinsic curvature is the four-dimensional one because $R$ is fixed. Integration of (U.44u.1) gives
$$
S_4=\frac{\bar M^2}{2}\int_B\sqrt{-g}\,R_g
-\frac{12\bar M^2}{2}\int_B\sqrt{-g}\,
g^{\mu\nu}g_{FS}(\partial_\mu[z],\partial_\nu[z])
+\bar M^2\int_{\partial B}\epsilon_{\partial}\sqrt{|\gamma_{\partial B}|}\,K .
\tag{U.44u.5}
$$
Here $\epsilon_{\partial}=g(n,n)$ on each smooth nonnull boundary portion. On the retained timelike slab boundaries it is $+1$. For $v\in\mathcal S_{-4}$ horizontal, its positive kinetic quadratic form is $12\bar M^2 h(v,v)/2=\bar M^2 h(v,Lv)/2$. This supplies the normalization in item 2 of Definition U.44b from the physical action. It uses the unit radius of the declared target, the winding curvature, the exchange symmetry, and the measured Bloch map. The Rayleigh eigenvalue agrees with the response and was not used to set either input stiffness.

*One proper slab and boundary charge.* Use the flat constant-$N_2$ product reference, with a proper external slab of length $L$, proper transverse area $A$, and the independently calibrated fractional shear and Hopf arclength of Theorem U.44k. In the same proper time the tangent tensor and scalar actions are of that theorem's form, with coefficients $B_{\rm shear}=\bar M^2$ and $B_{\rm Hopf}=12\bar M^2$. The retarded two-endpoint forces are consequently $A\bar M^2\mathcal N_L(z)$ and $12A\bar M^2\mathcal N_L(z)$, with the same outward derivatives, static opposite-end displacement, and spatial volume $AL$. For the finite spatial regulator of Theorem U.44n, apply the same action discretization to these two coefficients, with common lattice spacing, endpoint clock, preparation prescription and volume weight. Its two continuum comparisons and complete finite vacuum responses apply to these tangent fields with their coefficients now fixed by (U.44u.1)–(U.44u.5). The C64 calibration used for the response comparison still uses those derived source coefficients and the explicit regulator gain. It does not establish a microscopic C64 origin of the winding or target action.

The exact incoming-wave metric of Theorem U.44o also belongs to this source. Keep its incoming proper clock and transverse period normalization and use its two independent commands $\theta(u)$ and $d(u)$ with the image (U.44u.4) for the latter. The scalar equation holds on this null profile, and (U.44u.3) with the Ricci component computed in (U.44o.1) gives
$$
-2\frac{a''(u)}{a(u)}=(\theta'(u))^2+12(d'(u))^2 .
\tag{U.44u.6}
$$
The incoming conditions $a=1$, $a'=0$ fix the solution on a retained positive-area interval. Its uplift by the exact product equations retains all eight-dimensional fields with fixed internal radius. The measured transverse area $\mathcal A(u)=A_0a(u)^2$ gives $-2(\sqrt{\mathcal A})''/\sqrt{\mathcal A}$. Equal nonzero derivative profiles in separate shear and Hopf runs therefore have a focusing ratio of exactly $12$ at their common affine time, with the same incoming area and volume. The affine coordinate inherits its scale from the incoming proper clock as in Theorem U.44o. This boundary area response and the linearized two-endpoint forces are comparisons of the same classical action.

On the flat reference the stationary gravitational boost charge is that of the eight-dimensional Einstein term. A cross section of external area $\mathcal A$ lifts to $\mathcal A\times S^4$ with area $\mathcal A V_4$ and the same unit boost in the external normal plane. The minimally coupled $\sigma$ terms contain no curvature derivative. Thus the charge normalized as in Theorem U.44o is $2\pi M_8^6\mathcal A V_4=2\pi\bar M^2\mathcal A$. This is the same gravitational coefficient as the shear force, in the same normal proper clock and transverse area. It supplies the stationary geometric boundary anchor. An operational entropy/channel realization on the microscopic carrier remains a distinct input.

*Dependence on the winding source.* The derivation extends to $B\times S^n$, $n\ge2$, with the two unit round $S^n$ targets and the same exchange symmetry. The reference gives $\Lambda_{4+n}=0$ and $\kappa/M_{4+n}^{n+2}=n-1$ by the same internal equation. The unit equatorial $S^2$ and Bloch pullback give $\lambda^2=4(n-1)$. If exchange is removed, the first target stiffness is fixed by the internal reference equation while the second may vary independently without changing that reference. Thus the eight-dimensional source and its exchange symmetry have identifiable physical roles in the coefficient. The four-dimensional vacuum-torus obstruction is avoided by the distinct positive-curvature matter target. The present proof supplies neither a selection of the higher-dimensional source by PU nor stability of all omitted internal modes. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44v"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44v-dynamical-internal-radius-and-finite-null-area-balance-on-the-winding-source"></a>**Theorem U.44v (Dynamical Internal Radius and Finite Null-Area Balance on the Winding Source).** Keep the eight-dimensional action, both unit targets, the winding, and the coefficients of Theorem U.44u. The round internal radius can be dynamical in a consistent reduction. In the four-dimensional Einstein frame its logarithmic radius has kinetic coefficient $12\bar M^2$, equal to the coefficient of the Hopf arclength. On the unchanged eight-dimensional action there exist a pure radius pulse and a pure Hopf pulse with the same incoming state, incoming clock, and entire lifted transverse area history at the same true eight-dimensional affine parameter. The two histories have distinct proper internal radius and distinct matter flux. On a finite incoming null segment the area functional with the stationary charge coefficient differs from the affine-weighted matter-plus-shear flux by an explicit strictly positive expansion term for every nonconstant area history.

*Consistent round reduction.* Fix a reference radius $R_0>0$, write $V_4=R_0^4\operatorname{Vol}(S^4,\gamma)$ and $\bar M^2=M_8^6V_4$, and let
$$
\mathsf g=e^{-4\rho(x)}g(x)\oplus R_0^2 e^{2\rho(x)}\gamma(y),\qquad
N_1(x,y)=y,\qquad N_2(x,y)=N_2([z(x)])
\tag{U.44v.1}
$$
with the Bloch embedding of Theorem U.44u. The internal radius is $R_0e^\rho$. All differential operators without a metric subscript in this reduction use $g$. Set $\hat g=e^{-4\rho}g$ and $r=R_0e^\rho$. The warped metric has horizontal Ricci tensor $\operatorname{Ric}(\hat g)-4r^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_{\hat g}r$ and vertical Ricci tensor $(3-r\Box_{\hat g}r-3|dr|_{\hat g}^2)\gamma$. Its mixed components vanish. In four external dimensions the conformal Ricci formula gives
$$
\operatorname{Ric}_{\mu\nu}(\mathsf g)
=\operatorname{Ric}_{\mu\nu}(g)-12\,\partial_\mu\rho\,\partial_\nu\rho
+2\Box_g\rho\,g_{\mu\nu},\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}(\mathsf g)=(3-R_0^2e^{6\rho}\Box_g\rho)\gamma_{ij}.
\tag{U.44v.2}
$$
For the vertical identity, $\Box_{\hat g}\rho=e^{4\rho}(\Box_g\rho-4|d\rho|_g^2)$ and $r^{-1}\Box_{\hat g}r=\Box_{\hat g}\rho+|d\rho|_{\hat g}^2$. For the horizontal identity, conformal transformation gives $\operatorname{Ric}(\hat g)=\operatorname{Ric}(g)+4\operatorname{Hess}_g\rho+8d\rho\otimes d\rho+(2\Box_g\rho-8|d\rho|_g^2)g$, and $r^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}_{\hat g}r=\operatorname{Hess}_g\rho+5d\rho\otimes d\rho-2|d\rho|_g^2g$. The two sphere equations hold precisely when the external Bloch field solves its ordinary wave-map equation: the first sphere Laplacian and its squared gradient have the same radius factor, and the external inverse metric cancels the external conformal factor in the total volume density. The vertical equation in (U.44u.2) gives $\Box_g\rho=0$, and the horizontal equation gives
$$
\operatorname{Ric}(g)=12\,d\rho\otimes d\rho+12[z]^*g_{FS}.
\tag{U.44v.3}
$$
These equations check every component of the original equations.

The lifted volume density contains the factor $R_0^4e^{-4\rho}$. Tracing (U.44v.2) gives a bulk derivative $4\Box_g\rho$ in the reduced Einstein density, and the internal curvature term cancels the winding at every radius. For a smooth nonnull outer boundary with four-dimensional normal $n$, the lifted normal is $e^{2\rho}n$ and the lifted extrinsic curvature is $e^{2\rho}(K-2n(\rho))$. The boundary measure has inverse factor $e^{-2\rho}$. Thus the lifted Gibbons–Hawking–York term cancels the bulk divergence, including the sign of the outward normal in the divergence theorem. The reduced action is
$$
S_4=\frac{\bar M^2}{2}\int\sqrt{-g}
\bigl(R_g-12|d\rho|_g^2-12\,\operatorname{tr}_g [z]^*g_{FS}\bigr)
+\bar M^2\int_{\partial B}\epsilon_\partial\sqrt{|\gamma_\partial|}\,K.
\tag{U.44v.4}
$$
Its constant-radius branch is the retained sector of Theorem U.44u. The dynamical radius has zero potential and is a physical extra direction when its data are released.

*Coincident area histories at the same affine parameter.* Use the transverse torus, incoming proper-clock normalization, and Rosen metric of Theorem U.44o for $g$. Write $u$ for the four-dimensional affine coordinate and set the shear command to zero. For any $\rho(u)$ and Hopf geodesic command $d(u)$ constant before launch, the scalar equations hold, and (U.44v.3) gives $-2a_{uu}/a=12(\rho_u^2+d_u^2)$, with $a=1$, $a_u=0$ on the incoming flat region. Denote the second Rosen coordinate by $w$, so the longitudinal metric is $-2\,du\,dw$. A lifted generator with fixed $w,x,y$ and fixed internal point has eight-dimensional affine parameter $v$ given by $dv/du=e^{-4\rho(u)}$, with $v=u$ before launch. The lifted screen section has area
$$
\mathcal A(v)=A_0 V_4\,a(u(v))^2.
\tag{U.44v.5}
$$
Indeed the external two-dimensional area is multiplied by $e^{-4\rho}$, and the internal four-dimensional area by $e^{4\rho}$. This cancellation concerns the physical area of the full screen, without identifying the two factors separately.

For the radius run let $d=0$. Express the affine coordinates as numerical values in one fixed incoming clock unit, and use $\rho_u=\varepsilon e^{-1/u}$ for $u>0$ and zero for $u\le0$, with $\varepsilon>0$. Retain a fixed finite interval after launch, and take $\varepsilon$ small enough that $a>0$ throughout by continuity of the linear equation for $a$. Then $\rho_u\ge0$ and $a_u\le0$. In the Hopf run fix $\rho=0$ and define the Hopf command by its derivative in the common eight-dimensional affine clock,
$$
\frac{d d_{\rm H}}{dv}
=e^{4\rho}\rho_u
\left(1-\frac{2a_u}{3a\rho_u}\right)^{1/2}
\tag{U.44v.6}
$$
with all quantities on the right evaluated in the radius run at $u(v)$ and the derivative set to zero before launch. It is real and smooth. In fact for $u>0$ the nonnegative quantity $-a_u/\rho_u$ is
$$
6\varepsilon u^2e^{-1/u}\int_0^\infty
e^{-2t}(1+ut)^{-2}a\bigl(u/(1+ut)\bigr)\,dt .
\tag{U.44v.7}
$$
This follows by integrating $a_{uu}=-6\rho_u^2 a$ and substituting $1/s=1/u+t$. Differentiation under the integral to any finite order near $u=0$ is bounded by an integrable exponential times a polynomial in $t$. Thus the expression extends smoothly and flatly by zero. Decreasing $\varepsilon$ if needed keeps the Hopf field in its nominated chart. If $L>0$ is the chosen upper endpoint in $u$, positivity and the bound $a\le1$ imply $a\ge 1-3\varepsilon^2L^2$ and $|a_u|\le 6\varepsilon^2L$ by integrating the equation. These finite bounds and quadrature of the linear equation give a positive calibrated separation margin in the internal-distance readout below.

By the affine-clock derivative rule,
$$
-2\,\frac{d^2a(u(v))/dv^2}{a(u(v))}
=e^{8\rho}\left(12\rho_u^2-8\rho_u a_u/a\right)
=12\left(\frac{d d_{\rm H}}{dv}\right)^2 .
\tag{U.44v.8}
$$
The fixed-radius Hopf run has this same equation and the same incoming data, hence identical $a$ as a function of true eight-dimensional affine time. Its lifted area is (U.44v.5). The two commands and preparations can be compared at any specified $v>0$ in the retained interval. The radius run has $\rho>0$, so the internal antipodal proper distance is $\pi R_0e^\rho$, while in the Hopf run it is $\pi R_0$. Their matter null Ricci contractions from (U.44u.2) are respectively zero and $12(dd_{\rm H}/dv)^2$. A single finite proper internal-distance readout separates the two runs whenever its two error radii sum to less than $\pi R_0(e^\rho-1)$. The full lifted area alone has the same record at every time.

*Finite null balance with the stationary charge normalization.* Let $\Theta=d\log\mathcal A/dv$ and let $\sigma^2$ be the sum of squared eigenvalues of the trace-free optical deformation tensor of the six-dimensional screen. Let $k=\partial_v$ be its affinely normalized generator. For the lifted Rosen family the twist is zero. Its logarithmic screen scale factors are $\log a-2\rho\pm\theta/\sqrt2$ in the two external directions and $\rho$ in each of the four internal directions, up to constants. Taking derivatives in $v$ gives the optical tensor eigenvalues, and subtracting their mean gives
$$
\Theta=2\frac{\dot a}{a},\qquad
\sigma^2=\dot\theta^2+12\left(\dot\rho-\frac{\dot a}{3a}\right)^2,\qquad
\operatorname{Ric}(\mathsf g)(k,k)=12\dot d^{\,2}.
\tag{U.44v.9}
$$
Here dots use the true eight-dimensional affine parameter. In particular equality of the area histories of the two runs is compatible with distinct matter and shear parts. The optical equation is $\dot\Theta=-\Theta^2/6-\sigma^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\mathsf g)(k,k)$, equivalently
$$
\ddot{\mathcal A}=\mathcal A\left(\tfrac56\Theta^2-\sigma^2-\operatorname{Ric}(\mathsf g)(k,k)\right).
$$
This equation also follows by differentiating (U.44v.5) and using (U.44v.3) with the affine-clock conversion. Define the finite-area functional $\mathcal S(v)=2\pi M_8^6\mathcal A(v)$, normalized by the stationary charge of Theorem U.44u. For any retained positive-area segment $[0,v_f]$ starting with $\Theta(0)=0$, two integrations give the exact identity
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal S(0)-\mathcal S(v_f)
={}&\int_0^{v_f}(v_f-v)\,\mathcal S(v)
\left[\sigma^2+\operatorname{Ric}(\mathsf g)(k,k)\right]\,dv\\
&-\frac56\int_0^{v_f}(v_f-v)\,\mathcal S(v)\Theta(v)^2\,dv .
\end{aligned}
\tag{U.44v.10}
$$
The second integral is strictly positive for every smooth nonconstant area history. With this normalization and affine weight the flux integral is therefore strictly larger than the loss of the finite-area functional. For a stationary-radius, shear-free weak Hopf pulse of amplitude $\varepsilon$, $\Theta=O(\varepsilon^2)$ on a fixed positive-area interval, so the expansion term is $O(\varepsilon^4)$ while the flux starts at order $\varepsilon^2$. The finite identity gives the differential limit and identifies the extra term required at finite amplitude. It uses the geometric stationary charge coefficient and supplies no microscopic entropy instrument. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44w"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44w-winding-source-linear-gap-and-hopf-direction-identifiability"></a>**Theorem U.44w (Winding-Source Linear Gap and Hopf Direction Identifiability).** Use the full eight-dimensional action of Theorem U.44u on the flat external reference times the round internal sphere of radius $R_0>0$. Release all internal linearized metric and sphere-field fluctuations. On the complete flat external product, the gauge-invariant linearized spectrum has no negative squared mass. Every mode that varies over the internal sphere has squared mass at least $4/R_0^2$, and the bound is attained by a physical tensor mode. The internal-constant sector consists of the four-dimensional graviton, the round radius mode of Theorem U.44v and four massless polarizations of the second sphere field. Only two of those polarizations are tangent to the nominated Hopf sphere. On the full nonlinear action, a Hopf geodesic command and a normal geodesic command with the same unit-target arclength can give identical spacetime metrics and fluxes at fixed internal radius. A target readout distinguishes them, while all geometric area histories and stationary charge coefficients agree.

*Linearized equations in winding gauge.* Write $\gamma_R=R_0^2\gamma$ for the round internal metric, $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ for the flat external metric and $\nabla$ for the product connection. Greek indices are external and lower case Latin indices are internal. The differential of $N_1(y)=y$ identifies the internal tangent bundle with its pullback target tangent bundle. For any smooth linear perturbation of $N_1$, an internal infinitesimal diffeomorphism therefore sets $\delta N_1=0$ everywhere, including the full space of vector spherical harmonics. The background $N_2$ is constant, so its four-component tangent perturbation $\psi=\delta N_2$ is invariant under the linearized diffeomorphisms. Its equation is
$$
(\Box_4+\Delta_{\gamma_R})\psi=0,\qquad
\Box_4=-\partial_t^2+\sum_{a=1}^3\partial_{x_a}^2,
\tag{U.44w.1}
$$
and it has no linearized stress in the metric equation. In winding gauge the right side of the trace-reversed metric equation (U.44u.2) is unchanged, since $\Lambda_8=0$ and the first pullback tensor is fixed as a covariant tensor. Thus $\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}=0$.

For the metric perturbation $h$ put $B_A=\nabla^C h_{CA}-\tfrac12\nabla_A(\operatorname{tr}h)$. The wave-map equation for $N_1$ is the contracted difference between the domain connection with an internal upper index and the fixed target connection on the internal coordinates. The background difference vanishes. Its variation is $-\gamma_R^{ij}B_j$ in local target coordinates. Hence the field equation gives $B_i=0$. The residual gauge freedom has internal component zero. Under an external infinitesimal diffeomorphism $\xi_\mu(x,y)$ the external $B_\mu$ changes by $(\Box_4+\Delta_{\gamma_R})\xi_\mu$, and $B_i$ stays fixed. Solve this linear inhomogeneous wave equation on the flat external product with the compact sphere to impose $B_\mu=0$. Equivalently one may use smooth Cauchy data and a harmonic-by-harmonic solution. The remaining gauge transformations solve the homogeneous equation. These operations use no spectral projection onto the Hopf plane or removal of a physical internal degree of freedom.

With $B=0$, the variation of Ricci is the Lichnerowicz expression
$$
2\delta\operatorname{Ric}_{AB}
=-\nabla^C\nabla_C h_{AB}
-2R_{\mathrm{ACBD}}h^{CD}
+\operatorname{Ric}_A{}^C h_{CB}
+\operatorname{Ric}_B{}^C h_{CA}.
\tag{U.44w.2}
$$
This follows by varying the Levi-Civita connection and commuting the covariant derivatives. Set $K=R_0^{-2}$, $\tau=\gamma_R^{ij}h_{ij}$ and $t_{ij}=h_{ij}-(\tau/4)\gamma_{R,ij}$. The only nonzero background curvature is internal, with $\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}=3K\gamma_{R,ij}$ and $R_{ikjl}h^{kl}=K(\gamma_{R,ij}\tau-h_{ij})$. Thus the equations for the four blocks of $h$ are $\Box_4 h=\mathcal L h$, with respective internal operators
$$
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{block}&\mathcal L\\ \hline
h_{\mu\nu}&-\Delta_{\gamma_R}\\
h_{\mu i}&\nabla^*\nabla+3K\\
\tau&-\Delta_{\gamma_R}\\
t_{ij}&\nabla^*\nabla+8K .
\end{array}
\tag{U.44w.3}
$$
Here $\nabla^*\nabla$ is the nonnegative connection Laplacian on the indicated internal tensor bundle. In particular the scalar shift on the internal trace cancels exactly. The residual constraints $B_A=0$ can restrict these block solutions. Each block equation already bounds the support of any external plane-wave solution, so imposing the constraints cannot introduce negative or lower squared masses.

*Gap, attainment and massless fields.* The round-sphere scalar eigenvalues are $\ell(\ell+3)K$ for $\ell=0,1,\ldots$, obtained by restricting homogeneous harmonic polynomials on $\mathbb R^5$. This gives the scalar gap $4K$. The trace-free tensor operator is at least $8K$. The mixed operator is the Hodge Laplacian on one-forms by the Weitzenböck formula. On exact forms it has the positive scalar spectrum. On a co-closed one-form $\alpha$ one has
$$
\int_{S^4}|\nabla_i\alpha_j+\nabla_j\alpha_i|^2\,dV
=2\int_{S^4}\bigl(|\nabla\alpha|^2-3K|\alpha|^2\bigr)\,dV.
\tag{U.44w.4}
$$
This is integration by parts in the cross term and commutation of derivatives, using $\nabla^i\alpha_i=0$. The rough Laplacian is therefore at least $3K$ on that summand, giving Hodge gap at least $6K$. There are no harmonic one-forms, also by the positive Ricci term in the Weitzenböck formula. Hodge decomposition and (U.44w.1)–(U.44w.3) give the claimed bound on every internal nonconstant or mixed physical mode.

To attain it, take a first scalar harmonic $Y$ and an external massive transverse traceless plane-wave tensor $H_{\mu\nu}$ with $\Box_4 H=4K H$, and set $h_{\mu\nu}=YH_{\mu\nu}$ with all other components zero. The trace and divergence give $B_A=0$, and (U.44w.3) holds in every block. In the external rest frame the nonzero spatial traceless tensor components cannot be generated by a gauge change, since a gauge term in the external block is $\partial_\mu\xi_\nu+\partial_\nu\xi_\mu$ and the spatial momentum is zero. The mode is a physical massive spin-two excitation.

For squared mass zero, the scalar blocks are constant on the sphere, and the mixed and trace-free blocks vanish. In the internal trace write $h_{ij}=2\rho(x)\gamma_{R,ij}$, with $\Box_4\rho=0$. Define $H_{\mu\nu}=h_{\mu\nu}+4\rho\eta_{\mu\nu}$. Its linearized de Donder divergence on the external metric is exactly the external $B_\mu$ of the eight-dimensional perturbation, because the trace $8\rho$ from the internal block is canceled by this external conformal redefinition. Thus $H$ is the ordinary linearized massless graviton with its residual external diffeomorphism gauge. The separate scalar $\rho$ is the round radius field of (U.44v.4). The remaining four components are the internal-constant tangent components of $\psi$ in (U.44w.1), with kinetic coefficient $3\bar M^2$ in unit-target arclength by the original $\sigma$ term. They include the two normal polarizations of the nominated Hopf sphere. This classifies the massless sector and the sharp nonzero mass threshold. The argument concerns linearized frequencies about the stated flat product.

*A fixed-radius nonlinear area collision.* Let $p$ be the common incoming value of $N_2$ in the equatorial sphere. Take unit tangent vectors $b_\parallel$ and $b_\perp$ at $p$, with $b_\parallel$ tangent to the Hopf sphere and $b_\perp$ normal to it. For a real command $s(u)$ which is zero on the incoming flat segment, use the two exact geodesic maps
$$
N_2^\parallel(u)=\cos s(u)\,p+\sin s(u)\,b_\parallel,\qquad
N_2^\perp(u)=\cos s(u)\,p+\sin s(u)\,b_\perp .
\tag{U.44w.5}
$$
The target isometry fixing $p$ rotates one direction into the other. Each map gives the same pullback tensor $(s'(u))^2\,du\otimes du$. With zero shear and fixed radius, the common metric has $-2a''/a=3(s')^2$ and the same incoming area and proper affine clock, by (U.44u.2). Both full eight-dimensional solutions therefore have the same metric, matter stress, lifted null-area history, stationary boost-charge normalization and finite flux balance of Theorem U.44v. The marked Hopf arclength in the tangent run is $d=s/2$ by (U.44u.4). The comparison is a symmetry of the full action even with the internal radius held fixed.

If the plane is physically marked, a target readout in the fixed direction $b_\perp$ has values zero and $\sin s$ in the two runs. At a specified point with $0<|s|<\pi/2$, error radii whose sum is less than $|\sin s|$ certify the separation. Every readout that factors through the common spacetime metric, screen area and stress assigns the same response to the two histories. Consequently the internal mass gap justifies excluding nonconstant internal modes below its threshold in the linear comparison, but it leaves the two massless normal target directions active. An area service claiming Hopf-specific response must use a physical restriction of the source and its commands or retain a target-sensitive readout. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44x"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44x-coherent-boundary-information-and-weighted-area-on-the-winding-source"></a>**Theorem U.44x (Coherent Boundary Information and Weighted Area on the Winding Source).** Keep the fixed-radius winding action of Theorem U.44u, the incoming proper clock, and the proper transverse torus of area $A_0$. In the quadratic vacuum of its transversely constant fields on the flat external normal line, an independently calibrated shear command and a Hopf geodesic command have a common finite null-interval current construction. Their coherent relative entropies and the Fisher informations of one binary Ramsey instrument have ratio $12$ for equal nonzero physical command profiles. The same action's nonlinear geometric responses have that ratio in the second variation of a finite weighted area functional with the stationary charge coefficient. A uniform finite-amplitude error follows from the optical equation. The comparison uses the marked shear and Hopf directions, with the other independent quadratic modes in their vacuum.

*One physical normalization for the current.* Let $s$ be the normal spatial coordinate on the incoming flat reference, and use $u=t-s$ with the proper-clock normalization of Theorem U.44o. Consider separately either the nominated transverse traceless shear coordinate $q=\theta$ or the physical Fubini–Study geodesic coordinate $q=d$. Integrating the quadratic action of Theorems U.44k and U.44u over the same proper transverse torus gives the real massless action
$$
\frac{A_0B}{2}\int dt\,ds\bigl((\partial_t q)^2-(\partial_s q)^2\bigr),
\qquad B=\bar M^2\ \text{or}\ 12\bar M^2 .
\tag{U.44x.1}
$$
The canonical field is $\varphi=\sqrt{A_0B}\,q$. Its right-moving derivative $j=\partial_u\varphi$ is the vacuum chiral current, with the zero mode excluded by taking the derivative. This is the transversely constant sector of the given quadratic action on the normal line, rather than an imposed boundary temperature. The unused chirality, normal target modes and radius mode are orthogonal free components of the quadratic theory. Putting their states equal to the reference vacuum makes their relative entropy contributions zero. The nonlinear geometric comparisons below fix the radius and use the exact same two marked geodesic commands. The mode exclusions refer to these specified preparations and solutions, rather than an identification of distinct physical modes with gauge.

Fix a real nonzero $f\in C_c^\infty(0,L)$, with $L>0$, as the common command profile $q(u)=\delta f(u)$. Use the vacuum reference of (U.44x.1) and its coherent displacement by the right-moving solution $\sqrt{A_0B}\delta f$. The compact smooth profile gives a finite one-particle Weyl displacement and localizes its current shift in $I=(0,L)$. The canonical null energy of the displaced right-mover above vacuum is $A_0B\delta^2 f'(u)^2$. The local vacuum modular flow on the chiral interval is the Möbius flow with weight $w(u)=u(L-u)/L$. Its coherent relative entropy therefore is
$$
D_I(B,\delta)=2\pi A_0B\,\delta^2\int_0^L w(u)f'(u)^2\,du .
\tag{U.44x.2}
$$
This uses the vacuum interval formula for a compactly supported coherent current displacement. Equivalently, the displacement is local, so the Araki formula for a local Weyl conjugation gives the difference of modular energy, and the Möbius generator has local stress weight $2\pi w$. Both expressions use the canonical scalar stress of (U.44x.1); the factor $A_0B$ comes from its symplectic form. See Garbarz and Palau (2023).

*Binary operational measurement in the same vacuum.* Take the real current test $g=f'$ in the fixed $u$ units, and write $J(g)=\int g(u)j(u)\,du$. With Fourier transform $\widehat g(k)=\int e^{-iku}g(u)\,du$, the canonical mode expansion of $\varphi$ gives the vacuum variance and the coherent mean
$$
V=\int_0^\infty \frac{k}{4\pi}|\widehat g(k)|^2\,dk>0,\qquad
\mu=\sqrt{A_0B}\,\delta\,I_f,\qquad I_f=\int_0^L f'(u)^2\,du .
\tag{U.44x.3}
$$
The variance is identical in the two canonical current copies. The integral converges because $g$ is smooth and compactly supported, and is positive since $g$ is nonzero. Its normalization follows by expanding the right mover as $\int_0^\infty (a(k)e^{-iku}+a(k)^*e^{iku})\,dk/\sqrt{4\pi k}$ with $[a(k),a(k')^*]=\delta(k-k')$. For the bounded Weyl unitary $U=\exp(iJ(g)/\sqrt V)$ the exact coherent characteristic is $\langle U\rangle=e^{-1/2}e^{i\mu/\sqrt V}$.

Prepare a neutral qubit in its plus state, apply the controlled unitary with diagonal entries $1,U$, and measure Pauli $Y$ with the orientation giving the imaginary quadrature. This is a two-outcome instrument with Kraus operators $(I\mp iU)/2$ up to the corresponding outcome phases. Both branches are retained. The common calibrated gain is fixed by the vacuum variance before the driven test. The probabilities and Fisher information for the amplitude at zero are
$$
p_\pm=\frac{1\pm e^{-1/2}\sin(\mu/\sqrt V)}2,\qquad
\mathcal I_B(0)=e^{-1}A_0B\,\frac{I_f^2}{V}.
\tag{U.44x.4}
$$
The Fisher expression follows by direct differentiation of these Bernoulli probabilities. Every operation in the instrument is a bounded current or qubit operation on the declared test. It can be implemented as a local-algebra controlled gate with bounded generator $|1\rangle\langle1|\otimes\operatorname{Arg}U$ on the pulse support, whose norm is at most $\pi$ and whose action integral is at most $\pi$ in units $\hbar=1$ when multiplied by a nonnegative unit-integral switching profile. This is a specified probe access in the quadratic current algebra. It does not identify the detector with an unassisted gravitational boundary or erase its preparation and measurement costs.

The single current effect admits effective mode-approximation errors. For example the omitted vacuum variance above momentum $K>0$ is at most $\|g^{(m)}\|_1^2K^{2-2m}/[4\pi(2m-2)]$ for each integer $m>1$, by integrating the Fourier transform by parts. The omitted low interval $(0,k_0)$ is at most $\|g\|_1^2 k_0^2/(8\pi)$. Finite quadrature on $[k_0,K]$ gives enclosures for (U.44x.3), and the coherent shift can be bounded by the same one-particle Cauchy–Schwarz estimate on the omitted displacement and test modes. The same estimates apply to finite-dimensional approximations to their one-particle vectors in $L^2(\mathbb R_+)$, giving the finite mode comparison of the bounded Weyl probabilities. For repeated independent runs the binary sample mean has a confidence radius $\sqrt{\log(2/\zeta)/(2N)}$ at failure probability $\zeta$ for $N$ specimens. Within the first monotone sine arc this and the gain enclosure give a finite inverse error. The measured Fisher information is a finite-output distinguishability measure, while (U.44x.2) is a relative entropy on the interval algebra.

*Weighted geometric area and its error.* For either exact fixed-radius nonlinear pulse let $a(u)$ solve
$$
-2a''/a=(B/\bar M^2)\delta^2 f'(u)^2,\qquad
a(0)=1,\quad a'(0)=0,
\tag{U.44x.5}
$$
as in Theorem U.44u. On the fixed-radius branch the incoming-normalized true eight-dimensional affine clock is $u$. The lifted stationary-normalized area functional is $S(u)=S_0a(u)^2$ with $S_0=2\pi\bar M^2 A_0$. Define the geometric functional
$$
\mathcal G_B=\frac{2}{L}\int_0^L S(u)\,du-S(0)-S(L).
\tag{U.44x.6}
$$
Twice integrating by parts, using $w(0)=w(L)=0$, $w'(0)=1$, $w'(L)=-1$ and $w''=-2/L$, gives $\mathcal G_B=-\int_0^L w S''$. Direct differentiation of $S=S_0a^2$ and substitution of (U.44x.5) give the exact finite identity
$$
\mathcal G_B
=2\pi A_0B\,\delta^2\int_0^L w\,a^2 f'^2\,du
-2S_0\int_0^L w(a')^2\,du .
\tag{U.44x.7}
$$
This is also the finite weighted null balance of Theorem U.44v on this branch. Its negative last term is the net expansion correction after the fixed-radius screen shear contribution is kept.

Put $C=B/\bar M^2$ and suppose $C\delta^2 L I_f/2<1$. On any interval with positive $a$, the equation gives $0\le1-a\le C\delta^2 L I_f/2$ and $|a'|\le C\delta^2 I_f/2$ by integrating with $a\le1$. These bounds exclude a first zero of $a$ on $[0,L]$. Thus $1-a^2\le C\delta^2 L I_f$. Because $w\ge0$ and $\int_0^L w=L^2/6$, (U.44x.2) and (U.44x.7) give the certified comparison
$$
0\le D_I(B,\delta)-\mathcal G_B
\le S_0 C^2\delta^4\left[L I_f\int_0^L w f'^2\,du+\frac{L^2I_f^2}{12}\right].
\tag{U.44x.8}
$$
The leading coefficient of $\mathcal G_B$ is exactly the coherent relative-entropy coefficient. The ratio of those leading coefficients and of the binary Fisher informations is $12$, with the same command, proper time, transverse area, and physical field normalization. The full finite geometric functional differs by the bounded quartic terms. Equality of the quadratic coefficients does not identify the stationary absolute area entropy with either of these relative or classical information quantities. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44y"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44y-operational-capacity-per-unit-modular-work-on-the-winding-boundary"></a>**Theorem U.44y (Operational Capacity per Unit Modular Work on the Winding Boundary).** Use the marked quadratic current channel of Theorem U.44x on $I=(0,L)$, with independent preparations and recipients for different channel uses. A source symbol is a prescribed coherent pulse. The zero-cost symbol is the reference vacuum. Charge each pulse its dimensionless excess vacuum modular energy $D_I$ of (U.44x.2), and retain this cost separately from installation, repetition, measurement and elapsed time. The asymptotic classical capacity per unit of this work is exactly one nat. This holds already for the two-symbol alphabet consisting of vacuum and any one fixed nonzero smooth compactly supported pulse in the marked direction, including an arbitrarily weak one. For the same physical profile and amplitude in the Hopf and shear directions, the attainable information exponents per nonvacuum use have ratio $12$. This is a finite-output coding realization of the interval's relative coefficient on the winding source.

*States and cost converse.* Let $\mathcal M(I)$ be the von Neumann algebra generated by the Weyl currents of compactly supported real tests in $I$. Write $\omega_0$ for the vacuum and $\omega_f$ for its coherent translate by the specified pulse. The vacuum is faithful on this interval algebra by its standard real-subspace representation. Put $d_f=D(\omega_f\Vert\omega_0)$, which is positive and finite by (U.44x.2) for every nonzero such pulse. Relative entropies here are Araki relative entropies in nats. For a finite alphabet of pulse outputs, or finite words in independent such outputs, write $\omega_m$ for the output of message $m$ with probability $p_m$, $\overline\omega=\sum_m p_m\omega_m$, and $\sigma$ for the all-vacuum output. The exact information identity is
$$
\sum_m p_m D(\omega_m\Vert\sigma)
=\sum_m p_m D(\omega_m\Vert\overline\omega)+D(\overline\omega\Vert\sigma).
\tag{U.44y.1}
$$
This is the relative-entropy ensemble identity for normal states with finite average relative entropy. The first term on the right is the classical–quantum mutual information of the message label and recipient. Additivity makes the left side exactly the mean modular work of the words. Data processing bounds the information of any decoder's classical transcript by this mean work. For $M_{\rm code}$ equiprobable messages with average error $e$, Fano's bound gives
$$
(1-e)\log M_{\rm code}-h_2(e)
\le \mathbb E[\text{modular work}],
\tag{U.44y.2}
$$
where $h_2$ is the binary entropy. The units and zero of work are the same as in Theorem U.44x. See Donald (1986).

There is strict information loss relative to mean work for every nontrivial fixed finite coherent ensemble. To see this, take a real test supported in one channel use for which at least one constituent mean shift $\mu_m$ is nonzero. Such a test exists by choosing the derivative of that constituent's nonzero profile in that use. For all sufficiently small $t>0$, $\operatorname{Re}\sum_m p_m e^{it\mu_m}<1$. The vacuum Weyl expectation is strictly positive, so the corresponding cosine expectation of the mixture differs strictly from the vacuum. Thus $\overline\omega\ne\sigma$ and the last term in (U.44y.1) is positive. This strictness is a statement about a fixed code and leaves the asymptotic rate to be established.

*Local finite oscillator approximations.* The real smooth compact tests have a nondegenerate symplectic form given, up to the fixed canonical normalization, by $\int g h'$. A test symplectically orthogonal to all others has zero derivative distribution and hence vanishes by compact support. Choose a countable dense family of real compact smooth tests, for example an effective dense family of smooth bump approximants with rational data on successively smaller compact complements of the endpoints. Form an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional nondegenerate symplectic subspaces $V_j$ containing that family. To extend $V_j$, subtract the symplectic projection of the new test onto $V_j$. If the residual is nonzero, choose another compact test in the symplectic orthogonal complement with nonzero pairing and add the resulting two-dimensional symplectic plane. This is possible by nondegeneracy. The procedure can use rationally computable tests and strictly certified nonzero pairings, enumerating test pairs and skipping pairs whose dependence is already known from the chosen linearly independent compact tests. Alternatively at each stage enumerate all certified nondegenerate finite tuples, and enlarge their first finitely many spaces by finite symplectic completion. The latter construction suffices for effective searches without deciding equality of arbitrary real coefficients.

The regular Weyl representation of each $V_j$ generates a finite-number oscillator type-I factor $\mathcal M_j$ by the uniqueness of the finite-dimensional regular CCR representation, with the possible multiplicity space unaffected. These factors are actual subalgebras of $\mathcal M(I)$. Their union generates it because Weyl operators are strongly continuous in the current one-particle norm and the test family is dense in that norm. The restrictions of $\omega_0$ and $\omega_f$ have finite Gaussian covariance matrices and a finite displacement vector, computed by the current Gram and mean integrals of Theorem U.44x. The reference restriction is faithful because the full interval vacuum is faithful.

Relative entropy is monotone under these restrictions and
$$
D(\omega_f|_{\mathcal M_j}\Vert\omega_0|_{\mathcal M_j})
\ \uparrow\ d_f .
\tag{U.44y.3}
$$
For the convergence, use the variational expression for Araki relative entropy in terms of bounded simple functions with values in the algebra. For a fixed such test approximate its finitely many values in bounded strong-star topology by elements from the increasing union, using Kaplansky density. The evaluations of the quadratic terms by either normal state converge. Taking the supremum over tests proves the lower inequality in the limit, and restriction monotonicity gives the upper inequality. See Kosaki (1986).

At a fixed $j$ reduce further to a finite matrix recipient with one retained overflow result. In any fixed oscillator basis take projections $P_n$ onto increasing finite occupation rectangles, so $P_n\to I$ strongly. The algebra $P_n\mathcal M_jP_n\oplus\mathbb C(I-P_n)$ consists of a full finite matrix block and a scalar overflow block. These unital subalgebras increase and generate $\mathcal M_j$. The same variational argument shows that their two density matrices $\rho_{j,n}$ and $\sigma_{j,n}$ have relative entropies increasing to the value on $\mathcal M_j$. Compression retains the actual probability of each outcome, including the overflow. Consequently, for any $\varepsilon>0$ one can choose $j,n$ with
$$
d_f-\varepsilon<D(\rho_{j,n}\Vert\sigma_{j,n})\le d_f .
\tag{U.44y.4}
$$
For effective source pulses this choice has a finite certificate. The Gram and displacement integrals have the explicit tail bounds of Theorem U.44x. In symplectic coordinates on $V_j$, the finite matrix elements follow by integrating the Gaussian Weyl characteristic against the Weyl transforms of oscillator number-state matrix units, which are polynomials times Gaussians. The finite symplectic basis is obtained by the nonzero Gram pairings, and each integral has computable Gaussian tails because the finite covariance is strictly positive. The overflow entry is one minus the trace of the retained block. Positivity of the reference on this finite algebra certifies a strictly positive smallest eigenvalue at sufficient precision. Continuous functional calculus for $x\log x$, including its value zero at zero, and for the reference logarithm on its certified spectral interval give outward enclosures of the finite relative entropy. Searching the finite grades and precision together terminates by (U.44y.3)–(U.44y.4), with the independently computed $d_f$ as the upper bound. This argument supplies a finite verification without equating a truncated global Fock algebra with a local interval.

*Finite binary discrimination and coding.* For any finite matrix pair in (U.44y.4) and any $r<D(\rho_{j,n}\Vert\sigma_{j,n})$, the finite-dimensional quantum Stein lemma supplies, for sufficiently large $N$, a binary effect $T_N$ on $N$ copies with
$$
\alpha_N=1-\rho_{j,n}^{\otimes N}(T_N)\longrightarrow0,\qquad
\beta_N=\sigma_{j,n}^{\otimes N}(T_N)\le e^{-Nr}.
\tag{U.44y.5}
$$
For a finite code with any requested strict error margin, enumerate $N$ and rational positive contractions on the finite output algebra, using the matrix enclosures above to certify both inequalities with slack. Use an intermediate exponent strictly between $r$ and the finite relative entropy in the existence statement to obtain the slack for the second inequality. Full matrix effects may be replaced by their block restrictions to the actual finite algebra since the states are block diagonal. Pullback under the local compression gives a bounded local effect on the $N$ interval recipients, with the same probabilities. Its square-root dilation on a neutral qubit gives an actual two-outcome instrument. For example the block unitary with diagonal blocks $\sqrt{I-T_N}$ and off-diagonal blocks $\sqrt{T_N}$ with opposite signs has a bounded self-adjoint generator by functional calculus. Measurement of the qubit retains success and failure. This is bounded test access on the local current recipients. It may require a collective detector acting across the $N$ independent specimens. See Hiai and Petz (1991).

Now take $M_{\rm code}$ blocks of $N$ recipients. To encode a message, fill its nominated block with the fixed nonzero pulse and every other block with vacuum. Test each block by (U.44y.5), report the unique accepted block when there is one, and retain other patterns as decoding failures. The union bound gives error at most $\alpha_N+(M_{\rm code}-1)\beta_N$, and every word uses exactly $Nd_f$ of modular work. Choosing $M_{\rm code}=\lfloor e^{N(r-\delta)}\rfloor$ for $0<\delta<r$ gives vanishing error and limiting ratio $(r-\delta)/d_f$. Letting the declared finite approximation tolerance and the strict exponent margins decrease gives one nat per unit modular work, which (U.44y.2) makes sharp. This uses only finitely many specimens and one bit per tested block at each finite precision. The construction is the pulse-position comparison for a zero-cost reference output (Ding et al. 2019a).

For the physical shear and Hopf profiles of Theorem U.44x, $d_f$ has the common factor $2\pi A_0\delta^2\int_0^L w(f')^2$ times the respective $B$. Their limiting exponents per nonvacuum specimen therefore have ratio $12$. A small fixed pulse lies in the same positive-area branch and has the finite geometric comparison error of (U.44x.8). The capacity statement charges only the stated modular work. It gives neither finite information at zero time cost nor an absolute equilibrium entropy or a capacity law at fixed physical hardware and elapsed time. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44z"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44z-proper-energy-capacity-and-finite-pulse-resolution-on-the-winding-boundary"></a>**Theorem U.44z (Proper-Energy Capacity and Finite Pulse Resolution on the Winding Boundary).** Use the independently prepared quadratic boundary current and marked physical commands of Theorems U.44x and U.44y on the interval $(0,L)$. Charge a coherent pulse its excess energy in the incoming proper clock. The sharp classical capacity per unit of this physical pulse energy is $\pi L/2$ in units $\hbar=c=1$. No fixed nonzero smooth pulse attains the optimal energy efficiency. On every finite real profile bank the sharp capacity per energy is attained as a coding limit using one nonzero eigenprofile. A bound on root-mean-square frequency gives a strictly smaller universal efficiency. The proper-energy efficiencies are the same for shear and Hopf commands, although the costs and exponents for the same physical command have ratio $12$. A positive expense on every used window and a positive window duration impose the finite code bounds below.

*Physical energy and interval information.* Write $q(u)$ for any real smooth compactly supported command in $I=(0,L)$ and $B$ for the action coefficient in (U.44x.1). With the vacuum energy subtracted, its right-moving field energy in the incoming flat clock is
$$
E_B(q)=A_0B\int_0^L q'(u)^2\,du .
\tag{U.44z.1}
$$
Indeed the two derivatives in the Hamiltonian density of (U.44x.1) have equal magnitude on the right-moving solution, and the proper spatial slice gives $|ds|=du$. The quadratic current vacuum displaced by this solution has the same covariance and the stated classical excess energy. Its relative entropy to the vacuum on the interval is
$$
D_I(B,q)=2\pi A_0B\int_0^L w(u)q'(u)^2\,du,\qquad
w(u)=\frac{u(L-u)}{L},
\tag{U.44z.2}
$$
by Theorem U.44x. Thus for nonzero commands
$$
\frac{D_I(B,q)}{E_B(q)}
=\frac{\pi L}{2}-\frac{2\pi}{L}
\frac{\int_0^L (u-L/2)^2q'(u)^2\,du}{\int_0^L q'(u)^2\,du}.
\tag{U.44z.3}
$$
This is strictly less than $\pi L/2$, since a nonzero square-integrable derivative cannot concentrate on the single point $L/2$. The conversion from modular work to proper energy is therefore a geometric time weight, rather than a new gain chosen from a measured information response.

For any admitted family of pulse profiles containing vacuum, let $\mathcal C_E$ be the supremum of asymptotic reliably decoded nats per mean total pulse energy of a word. Different channel uses have independent preparations as in Theorem U.44y. Then
$$
\mathcal C_E=\sup_{q\ne0}\frac{D_I(B,q)}{E_B(q)} .
\tag{U.44z.4}
$$
For the upper bound, (U.44y.1) and data processing bound decoded information by the average sum of individual relative entropies, hence by the right side times the average pulse energy. For achievability fix any one nonzero admitted pulse and use the binary-block pulse-position code of Theorem U.44y. The work of its nonvacuum block in this comparison is exactly the number of copies times (U.44z.1), and the achieved information exponent per copy approaches (U.44z.2). The fixed pulse amplitude can be arbitrarily weak. This preserves the independently specified regime of the quadratic field and the controlled geometric comparison of (U.44x.8).

For unrestricted smooth compact profiles choose a fixed nonconstant $f\in C_c^\infty(-1,1)$ and set $q_b(u)=\delta_b f((u-L/2)/b)$ for $0<b<L/2$. Its normalized centered derivative second moment in (U.44z.3) is exactly $b^2\int x^2f'(x)^2\,dx/\int f'(x)^2\,dx$. One can take $\delta_b=c\,b$ with any fixed small $c>0$. Then both the peak derivative and the total pulse energy are bounded, and the positive-area small-amplitude test of Theorem U.44x holds for sufficiently small $b$. Taking $b\downarrow0$ proves the sharp value $\pi L/2$ together with nonattainment by any fixed pulse. Different profiles can approach the optimum even though no fixed smooth profile has exactly that relative entropy per energy.

*Exact finite profile comparison.* Take any linearly independent real profiles $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in C_c^\infty(I)$, with a source menu containing every sufficiently small nonzero amplitude in each direction of their linear span. Define the two independent Gram matrices
$$
G_{ij}=\int_0^L f_i'f_j'\,du,\qquad
W_{ij}=\int_0^L w f_i'f_j'\,du .
\tag{U.44z.5}
$$
The first is strictly positive because a compactly supported linear combination with zero derivative is zero. The second is strictly positive as well because $w>0$ inside $I$. For $q=\sum_j v_jf_j$, the efficiency in (U.44z.3) is $2\pi v^{\mathsf T}Wv/(v^{\mathsf T}Gv)$. Therefore the exact capacity per energy on this bank is
$$
2\pi\,\lambda_{\max}\bigl(G^{-1/2}WG^{-1/2}\bigr).
\tag{U.44z.6}
$$
Its optimal profile directions are precisely the inverse images under $G^{1/2}$ of the largest-eigenvalue eigenspace. Any such direction may be scaled to a nonzero permitted amplitude and used in (U.44z.4). Its positive gap from $\pi L/2$ is exactly $2\pi/L$ times the smallest generalized eigenvalue of the centered-moment Gram relative to $G$. The centered-moment Gram is positive definite for the same reason as the strict inequality in (U.44z.3). With effective profiles, quadrature and certified eigenvalue enclosures give an explicit finite interval for (U.44z.6), and the finite tests of Theorem U.44y certify any strictly smaller positive achievable rate per energy. A common finite bank and common proper-time and command units give the same generalized eigenvalues for the two sectors. For a fixed profile the Hopf energy and information exponent each are twelve times the shear values because both inherit their factor $B$ from the action.

*Root-mean-square frequency and a uniform gap.* Let $g=q'$, extend it by zero and impose an independently fixed root-mean-square frequency cap $\Omega>0$:
$$
\int_0^L |g'|^2\,du\le \Omega^2\int_0^L |g|^2\,du .
\tag{U.44z.7}
$$
This is the Fourier second-moment cap by Plancherel in the proper clock. It does not impose simultaneous compact frequency support. Integration by parts gives $\int g^2=-2\int (u-L/2)gg'$, with no boundary term. Cauchy–Schwarz and (U.44z.7) give the uniform inequality
$$
\frac{D_I(B,q)}{E_B(q)}
\le \frac{\pi L}{2}-\frac{\pi}{2L\Omega^2}.
\tag{U.44z.8}
$$
This holds on the entire nonempty smooth cap class whenever it is used. A sequence attaining the unrestricted efficiency must have unbounded root-mean-square frequency by the same inequality. The physical restriction can thus be tested on the actual pulse profile, independently of detector success or cosmological comparisons.

*Positive window expense and elapsed time.* Consider an experiment running $N$ independent uses of the interval channel, where every used window, including an empty one, occupies at least $L$ in the incoming clock. The windows are scheduled serially. Suppose each costs an independently fixed nonnegative base amount $E_{\rm base}$ in the same energy accounting, and every pulse has energy at most $E_{\max}<\infty$. Let $c_E$ be any upper bound for the applicable family from (U.44z.4), (U.44z.6) or (U.44z.8). Write $\overline E$ for the mean pulse energy of a word and $e$ for its average error. The exact finite Fano comparison is
$$
(1-e)\log M_{\rm code}-h_2(e)\le c_E\overline E,
\qquad 0\le\overline E\le N E_{\max}.
\tag{U.44z.9}
$$
The right side divided by the time is at most $c_E E_{\max}/L$. Dividing by $\overline E+NE_{\rm base}$ when that total is positive gives at most $c_E E_{\max}/(E_{\max}+E_{\rm base})$. Any extra receiver, preparation or reset expense only raises the denominator. These are finite resource upper bounds. The pulse-position construction of Theorem U.44y has $N_{\rm block}M_{\rm code}$ windows for $N_{\rm block}$ nonvacuum uses, so along its fixed-pulse coding limit its information rate per serial time tends to zero. With any fixed $E_{\rm base}>0$ its information per total expense also tends to zero. Thus the attainment in (U.44z.4) is an energy-efficiency limit with all empty windows retained. A sharp positive-time capacity at a fixed total-resource tariff is a different optimization. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44z1"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44z1-fixed-pulse-proper-time-and-total-expense-capacity"></a>**Theorem U.44z.1 (Fixed-Pulse Proper-Time and Total-Expense Capacity).** Keep the marked quadratic boundary current of Theorem U.44x and its independently prepared interval recipients. On each serial use of duration $L$ send either the vacuum or one fixed nonzero coherent pulse, with no prior shared entanglement and with collective decoding on the used recipients allowed. Let $E>0$ be the pulse's incoming proper energy and let $E_{\rm base}>0$ be the fixed charged expense of each use in the same units. Let $\omega_0,\omega_1$ be the two normal recipient states, $\omega_p=(1-p)\omega_0+p\omega_1$ and
$$
\chi(p)=(1-p)D(\omega_0\Vert\omega_p)+pD(\omega_1\Vert\omega_p),
\qquad d=D(\omega_1\Vert\omega_0).
\tag{U.44z.1.1}
$$
Here $D$ is Araki relative entropy on the actual interval algebra. With a mean pulse energy cap $P\ge0$ per use, set $p_{\max}=\min(1,P/E)$. The sharp proper-time capacity and the sharp efficiency per total expense on this serial-use model are
$$
\frac{\chi(\min\{1/2,p_{\max}\})}{L},
\qquad
\max_{0\le p\le p_{\max}}\frac{\chi(p)}{E_{\rm base}+pE},
\tag{U.44z.1.2}
$$
respectively. Without the cap use $p_{\max}=1$. Both are positive when $P>0$, and both have finite enclosures to any requested accuracy for effective source inputs. For $p_{\max}>0$ the expense efficiency has a unique maximizing pulse fraction in $(0,\min\{1/2,p_{\max}\}]$. For the same fixed physical profile in the shear and Hopf directions without a pulse-energy cap, their proper-time capacities have ratio strictly between $1$ and $12$.

*Single-use properties.* The current parity automorphism sends the coherent displacement to its negative and fixes the vacuum. Composing its action on states with displacement by the given pulse exchanges $\omega_0$ and $\omega_1$, with the same interval algebra. Thus $\chi(p)=\chi(1-p)$. It is strictly concave in $p$ on $[0,1]$. To see this, let $p=\lambda q+(1-\lambda)r$ with $0<\lambda<1$. The entropy ensemble identity (U.44y.1) for the two conditional ensembles gives
$$
\chi(p)-\lambda\chi(q)-(1-\lambda)\chi(r)
=\lambda D(\omega_q\Vert\omega_p)+(1-\lambda)D(\omega_r\Vert\omega_p).
\tag{U.44z.1.3}
$$
This is positive when $q\ne r$ because $\omega_0$ and $\omega_1$ are distinct. Those states are faithful and distinct by the vacuum standardness and the nonzero compact Weyl displacement in Theorem U.44x. All the entropies in (U.44z.1.3) are finite: each reference mixture with positive weights dominates its two constituent mixtures, and the relative entropy to the vacuum is finite by (U.44x.2). The bound $0\le\chi(p)\le h_2(p)$ gives continuity at the endpoints, where $\chi=0$. Thus $\chi$ has a unique unconstrained maximum at $1/2$ and increases up to that point. Its positive value for $0<p<1$ also follows directly from (U.44z.1.1). For the expense ratio, continuity on the compact feasible set gives a maximum. If two distinct points gave its positive maximum $c$, strict concavity of $\chi(p)-c(E_{\rm base}+pE)$ would give a larger ratio between them. No $p>1/2$ is optimal since $1/2$ has at least as large a numerator and a smaller denominator.

*Converse with time and expense charged.* On $N$ serial uses of total duration $NL$, let $p_i$ be the average pulse probability at position $i$, and $\overline p=N^{-1}\sum_i p_i$. Each word gives a product of the two states, with average pulse energy $N\overline pE$. Let $\rho$ be the average word state and $\rho_i=\omega_{p_i}$ its one-use marginals. Applying the entropy ensemble identity to the word ensemble with reference $\bigotimes_i\rho_i$ yields
$$
I(\mathrm{message}:\mathrm{recipient})
=\sum_i\chi(p_i)-D\!\left(\rho\ \middle\Vert\ \bigotimes_i\rho_i\right)
\le N\chi(\overline p).
\tag{U.44z.1.4}
$$
Indeed each word's relative entropy to the product reference is a sum of one-use terms, and its average is $\sum_i\chi(p_i)$. Positions with a deterministic letter contribute zero. This argument works on the tensor product of the actual interval algebras and requires no entropy difference between their vacuum density matrices. Data processing and Fano therefore give the finite bound
$$
(1-e)\log M_{\rm code}-h_2(e)\le N\chi(\overline p)
\tag{U.44z.1.5}
$$
for $M_{\rm code}$ equiprobable messages and average error $e$. Dividing by $NL$ or by $N(E_{\rm base}+\overline pE)$ gives the stated limiting upper bounds, with the positive expenses of all vacuum windows included.

*Uniform finite enclosures.* Use the actual finite oscillator and overflow subalgebras of Theorem U.44y. At any such finite grade $j$ let $\omega_{a,j}$ be the restricted states, $d_j=D(\omega_{1,j}\Vert\omega_{0,j})$, and $\chi_j(p)$ the finite ensemble quantity. The two exact ensemble identities with vacuum reference give
$$
\chi(p)=pd-D(\omega_p\Vert\omega_0),\qquad
\chi_j(p)=pd_j-D(\omega_{p,j}\Vert\omega_{0,j}).
$$
Data processing for the label–recipient mutual information gives the lower comparison, and data processing for the mixture term gives the upper comparison
$$
0\le \chi(p)-\chi_j(p)\le p(d-d_j)\qquad(0\le p\le1).
\tag{U.44z.1.6}
$$
The right side is a computable uniform defect because $d$ is evaluated on the original current and $d_j$ increases to it by (U.44y.3)–(U.44y.4). In particular no density-matrix cutoff for the whole interval is needed.

The one-variable optimization at a finite grade is effective. In its finite matrix dimension $D_j$, put $t=|p-q|$. The trace distance of the two mixtures is at most $t$. Coupling their spectra using the trace-norm eigenvalue perturbation inequality, and then applying the classical entropy bound for distributions of distance at most $t$, gives $|S(\omega_{p,j})-S(\omega_{q,j})|\le h_2(t)+t\log D_j$ for $0\le t\le1/2$. The two affine constituent entropy terms change by at most $t\log D_j$. Hence $|\chi_j(p)-\chi_j(q)|\le h_2(t)+2t\log D_j$. The expense denominator has an independent positive lower bound $E_{\rm base}$ and is affine, so this supplies an explicit mesh error for the finite ratio optimization. For example, its additional change from the denominator is at most $tE\log 2/E_{\rm base}^2$ since $\chi_j\le h_2\le\log 2$. Apply (U.44z.1.6) divided by the positive denominators to transfer the resulting enclosures to (U.44z.1.2). The actual optimum and the required strict subcapacity margins can therefore be certified with a finite source-grade and mesh search.

*Achievability by finite codes on the interval recipients.* At any rational $p$ strictly inside the admitted cap and any rate per use below $\chi(p)$, (U.44z.1.6) first provides a finite grade with $\chi_j(p)$ above the rate. The finite-dimensional classical–quantum coding theorem with the prescribed input composition supplies arbitrarily small average error at that rate, with the word pulse fraction tending to $p$. One may take constant composition with integer counts converging to $pN$ to meet the strict cap. Each finite code and its collective positive-operator-valued decoder can be verified by the finite matrices from Theorem U.44y. In particular enumerate finite codebooks of the required type and rational positive effects forming a complete finite decoder, and accept a strict average error inequality by outward enclosures. A small mixture with the uniform decoder gives a positive spectral margin for every effect and slack in the error target, so rational approximants that sum to the identity exist and preserve the strict bound. Pullback from the finite algebra makes the effects actual effects on the corresponding interval recipients, with the overflow retained. The finite square-root isometry into one pointer register per decoder alphabet and its unitary extension give a bounded recipient-algebra instrument of the same declared access type as in Theorem U.44y. The number of used windows and their expenses are exactly the ones in (U.44z.1.5). The elapsed-time convention is serial uses of duration $L$ with collective decoding on the stored recipients. Any separate decoder duration and cost must be included in a tariff that charges those resources. Taking rational $p$ to either optimizing fraction proves the lower bounds, also when the optimum lies at the cap. If $P=0$ only the reference word is admitted and both capacities are zero. See Holevo (1997).

*Hopf and shear comparison.* In canonical current units the fixed physical Hopf pulse has $\sqrt{12}$ times the displacement of the same shear pulse, while their vacuum laws coincide. In twelve independent copies of the shear current, an orthogonal change of the twelve field coordinates preserves both the vacuum covariance and the symplectic form. It takes the vector of twelve equal displacements to a displacement $\sqrt{12}$ times as large in one copy and vacuum in the other eleven. This is an interval algebra automorphism because it mixes only identical copies at the same smearing. Therefore the Holevo information of the Hopf binary alphabet at fraction $p$ equals the information of twelve copies of the shear alphabet conditional on one common binary message.

For $0<p<1$, write $\rho_{12}$ for this average word state and $\omega_p$ for its shear one-copy marginal. Equation (U.44z.1.4) gives the upper bound by $12\chi_{\rm shear}(p)$ with defect $D(\rho_{12}\Vert\omega_p^{\otimes12})$. The defect is positive: choose a bounded real current effect $F$ with distinct constituent expectations. The covariance of this effect in two distinct copies under $\rho_{12}$ is $p(1-p)(\omega_1(F)-\omega_0(F))^2>0$, whereas under the product average it is zero. Restricting the recipient to one copy gives the lower bound $\chi_{\rm Hopf}(p)\ge\chi_{\rm shear}(p)$. Equality would force equality of both constituent relative entropies to the average under restriction, because each loss is nonnegative and each letter has positive weight. The equality criterion for restriction of faithful normal states then gives one recovery map, with the common reference $\omega_p$, recovering both twelve-copy constituents from their one-copy marginals. Data processing in both directions would give equality of their pairwise relative entropy, contrary to its values $12d$ and $d>0$. Thus the lower inequality is strict too. At $p=1/2$ these inequalities prove the stated proper-time capacity ratio. See Petz (1986b). $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44z2"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44z2-absolute-entropy-test-on-a-winding-current-cut"></a>**Theorem U.44z.2 (Absolute Entropy Test on a Winding-Current Cut).** Use either canonically normalized chiral current of Theorem U.44x on the incoming flat reference, with its vacuum, fixed transverse area $A_0$ and proper affine coordinate $u$. At a fixed cut $u_*$, there are finite binary current measurements on its two sides whose vacuum transcripts have mutual information growing at least linearly in the number of tested scales. Every finite regulator with separate local output factors that reproduces those transcripts must have at least that much vacuum entropy on the inside factor. The stationary geometric charge of the cut is finite. For compact pulses lying strictly inside the cut, a split or finite regulator that retains the local Weyl conjugation has identical inside entropy for the vacuum and the pulse whenever those entropies exist. The exact fixed-radius geometric area at the same cut changes for these pulses. Thus the ordinary entropy of the retained current cannot supply the absolute stationary charge through a convergent raw entropy limit, or the driven area difference through a state-independent subtraction on the specified local regulators.

*Current measurements on a single proper cut.* Translate $u_*$ to zero for the vacuum test and let $g$ be a real, nonzero, nonnegative smooth function supported in $(1,2)$. Fix a proper length $r_1>0$. For $0<q\le 1/4$, use $r_j=r_1q^{j-1}$ and the tests $g_j^\pm(u)=g(\pm u/r_j)$ for $1\le j\le n$. These functions have disjoint supports on each side, and each side is contained in one bounded interval. Use the binary spectral projections of $J(g_j^\pm)$ onto its positive and negative half-lines. All these measurements commute because the chiral commutator is supported on coincident points. Their joint vacuum law is the sign law of a centered Gaussian vector by the Weyl characteristic functional. The variance of each current smearing is the common $V>0$ of (U.44x.3) with test $g$. In fact the rescaled Fourier transform is $r_j\widehat g(\pm r_j k)$, so its variance is independent of scale and side. The real covariance of any two tests $a,b$ with disjoint supports is
$$
\operatorname{Cov}(J(a),J(b))=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\iint\frac{a(x)b(y)}{(x-y)^2}\,dx\,dy .
\tag{U.44z.2a}
$$
To obtain (U.44z.2a) from the positive-frequency covariance in (U.44x.3), insert $e^{-\epsilon k}$ before integrating in $k$. The real part of $\int_0^\infty k e^{-\epsilon k-ik(x-y)}\,dk=(\epsilon+i(x-y))^{-2}$ tends uniformly to $-(x-y)^{-2}$ on the two supports. Each matched opposite-side pair therefore has the same correlation $-\rho$ with
$$
\rho=\frac{1}{4\pi V}\iint\frac{g(x)g(y)}{(x+y)^2}\,dx\,dy,\qquad 0<\rho<1 .
\tag{U.44z.2b}
$$
Strict positivity follows from $g\ge 0$. Equality in the variance Cauchy–Schwarz bound would require the positive-frequency vectors to be real multiples of one another. Reality extends that relation to the negative frequencies, which would make the two disjoint nonzero tests real multiples of one another. For standard bivariate Gaussians of correlation $-\rho$, the sign agreement probability is $b=1/2-\arcsin(\rho)/\pi$. This follows by writing the second Gaussian as $-\rho Z_1+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Z_2$ for independent standard Gaussians and taking the angular fraction of the agreement sectors. Thus each pair has binary mutual information $m=\log 2-h_2(b)>0$, where $h_2$ is binary entropy in nats.

*A uniform bound on the dependence within each side.* Two scales with ratio $q^k$ on the same side are at distance at least $r_{\rm large}(1-2q)$, and the product of their $L^1$ norms is $r_{\rm large}r_{\rm small}\|g\|_1^2$. By (U.44z.2a) the off-diagonal correlation at index difference $k$ has absolute value at most $Cq^k$ with $C=\|g\|_1^2/(\pi V)$. The correlation matrix $R$ on each side has diagonal $1$ and row sum of the absolute off-diagonal terms at most $\eta=2Cq/(1-q)$. Choose $q$ so that $\eta<1$ and $-\log(1-\eta)\le m/2$. This is a choice from the current's vacuum and the test shape, independent of the area charge. The spectrum of $R$ lies in $[1-\eta,1+\eta]$. The relative entropy of the normalized Gaussian vector on one side to its independent standard Gaussian marginals is $-\tfrac12\log\det R$, using the Gaussian density and $\operatorname{tr}R=n$. Data processing by the sign measurements bounds the total correlation of the binary vector on that side by $-\tfrac n2\log(1-\eta)$. Here total correlation is the sum of the marginal entropies minus the joint entropy. Write $X,Y$ for the two sign vectors. Subadditivity gives $H(X,Y)\le\sum_j H(X_j,Y_j)$, and each individual sign is fair. Consequently
$$
I(X:Y)\ge n m+ n\log(1-\eta)\ge \tfrac12 n m .
\tag{U.44z.2c}
$$

*Finite regulator bound.* Let a regulator on the same cut have separate tensor factors for the two readouts and reproduce the $2n$ sign law to total variation at most $\epsilon\le1/2$. Denote its inside vacuum density by $\sigma_{\rm in}$. Measurement on the outside gives an ensemble on the inside with mean $\sigma_{\rm in}$, so the Holevo bound gives $S(\sigma_{\rm in})\ge I_{\rm reg}(X:Y)$. The finite alphabet entropy continuity bound applied to $X$, $Y$ and $(X,Y)$ gives
$$
\log\dim\mathcal H_{\rm in}\ \ge\ S(\sigma_{\rm in})\ \ge\ \tfrac12 n m-4n\epsilon\log 2-3h_2(\epsilon) .
\tag{U.44z.2d}
$$
The three continuity bounds follow by coupling the laws with disagreement probability at most $\epsilon$ and bounding the conditional entropy by $h_2(\epsilon)+\epsilon\log(d-1)$ on an alphabet of size $d$. A sequence of regulators converging on every such finite local test family must have inside entropies diverging: for any desired bound choose $n$ first, then take the reproducing error small for that $n$. For a regulator resolving all tests down to proper scale $r_n$ with sufficiently small fixed $\epsilon$, (U.44z.2d) is a lower bound proportional to $1+\log(r_1/r_n)/|\log q|$ up to a constant. The charge on the same flat cut is $S_0=2\pi\bar M^2 A_0$ and is independent of $n$ and of the regulator.

*Vacuum subtraction for a pulse inside the cut.* Now take the cut at $u_*=L$ and the compact displacement $\delta f$ of Theorem U.44x, with $\operatorname{supp} f\Subset (0,L)$ and $\delta\ne 0$. Its Weyl unitary belongs to the inside current algebra. In any type-I split factor containing this unitary and contained in the inside algebra, or in a finite regulator in which the two prepared densities are related by the represented inside Weyl unitary, the pulse density on the factor is an inner conjugate of the vacuum density. Its entropy spectrum is identical. Every common state-independent subtraction therefore gives a zero difference whenever the subtracted entropies exist. In contrast the driven cut has $S(L)-S_0=S_0(a(L)^2-1)<0$ on the positive-screen branch of (U.44x.5): $a''=-\tfrac12(B/\bar M^2)\delta^2 f'^2 a$ is nonpositive and strictly negative on an open set before $L$, while $a(0)=1$ and $a'(0)=0$. The cut is at the same proper affine reading in the vacuum and driven records. This entropy test uses the fixed current algebra and its local Weyl preparations. An entropy incorporating an independent gravitational sector or a state-dependent factor assignment requires its own source and comparison law. $\square$

<a id="theorem-u44z3"></a>

<a id="theorem-u44z3-exact-exchange-symmetry-does-not-select-the-winding-branch-kinetic-ratio"></a>**Theorem U.44z.3 (Exact Exchange Symmetry Does Not Select the Winding-Branch Kinetic Ratio).** Keep the Einstein term, the two unit round $S^4$ targets, the independent $O(5)$ actions and their exchange, the degree-one winding reference, and the marked Bloch map of Theorem U.44u. Enlarge the matter action to smooth local functions of the two first-gradient invariants. Then every positive Hopf-to-shear coefficient occurs on the same fields and the same flat winding reference. The tensor coefficient, proper volume and clock, round-radius kinetic coefficient, stationary geometric charge, and sharp linear internal mass gap all agree across the family. Each member has an exact fixed-radius two-direction Hopf restriction for an open range of gradients, and the corresponding proper slab and calibrated null comparisons read its own coefficient. Thus microscopic selection of the winding-branch coefficient requires information beyond the stated exact symmetries and these reference tests.

*Exchange-invariant action on the same carrier.* Write $X_\alpha=\mathsf g^{AB}\partial_A N_\alpha\cdot\partial_B N_\alpha$, $\kappa=3M_8^6$ and $x_0=4/R_0^2$. The original matter density is $-\kappa(X_1+X_2)/2$. Take any $0<\epsilon<x_0/4$ and a smooth dimensionless function $H$ with $0\le H\le1$, $H=0$ on $[-\epsilon,\epsilon]$ and $H=1$ on $[x_0-\epsilon,x_0+\epsilon]$. These scales use the geometric winding radius, which can be set by the same product boundary data as in Theorem U.44u. For each $B>0$ add to the bulk matter density
$$
-\frac{B-\kappa}{2}\left[H(X_1)X_2+H(X_2)X_1\right] .
\tag{U.44z.3a}
$$
The coupling $B$ has the same units as $\kappa$. Equation (U.44z.3a) is invariant under the independent target rotations, exchange and eight-dimensional diffeomorphisms, with the same matter fields and Dirichlet data. It contains only first derivatives of the matter fields and adds no metric curvature dependence. Its equations have at most second derivatives. On the open jet region $|X_1-x_0|<\epsilon$ and $|X_2|<\epsilon$, the full density is exactly $-(\kappa X_1+B X_2)/2$. The identity holds on an open set of unconstrained metric and matter jets, so all first and higher variations there agree with that positive, minimally coupled two-field action. The exchange sends this region to the distinct region with the winding in the second field. There the exchanged local density has the same form with the two stiffnesses interchanged. These identities give the standard positive $\sigma$ kinetic forms and Einstein–wave-map hyperbolic principal system on the two reference neighborhoods. The theorem uses only those neighborhoods.

*Equal anchors and distinct physical responses.* The flat winding solution lies in the first region. Its Einstein equation fixes the first stiffness to $\kappa$ and the cosmological term to zero just as in (U.44u.2), since the second field is constant. All neighboring fixed-radius product histories with $N_1(y)=y$ and $|X_2|<\epsilon$ have the exact four-dimensional field equations
$$
\operatorname{Ric}_{\mu\nu}(g)=\frac{B}{M_8^6}\partial_\mu N_2\cdot\partial_\nu N_2,
\qquad \Box_gN_2+X_2N_2=0 .
\tag{U.44z.3b}
$$
The internal and mixed equations are still satisfied because the first map and its metric are unchanged and the second map depends only on external coordinates. The equatorial Bloch map is still totally geodesic and has pullback metric $4g_{FS}$. With $V_4=R_0^4\operatorname{Vol}(S^4,\gamma)$, the effective four-dimensional tensor coefficient is $\bar M^2=M_8^6V_4$ and the positive Hopf coefficient is $4BV_4$. Thus
$$
\lambda_B^2=\frac{4B}{M_8^6},\qquad B>0 .
\tag{U.44z.3c}
$$
The frame and physical arc length are the same for every $B$. In particular $B=\kappa$ gives $12$ and $B=\kappa/2$ gives $6$. The fixed shear and angle commands of Theorem U.44k therefore give the same proper tensor response and distinct proper Hopf responses. The finite spatial regulator of Theorem U.44n compares both on the same clock and cell volumes with the coefficients just derived. For each fixed-radius null command one has $X_2=0$ even at finite amplitude. Equation (U.44u.6) holds with $12$ replaced by $\lambda_B^2$, so the same affine and area calibrations distinguish the actions. The classical stationary charge is $2\pi\bar M^2\mathcal A$ because its curvature derivative receives no contribution from (U.44z.3a).

The round radius direction retains the Einstein-frame kinetic coefficient of Theorem U.44v, because on its entire pure-radius jet neighborhood $X_2=0$ and the matter variation reduces to that of the original winding. At the flat reference the unconstrained second variation in winding gauge is also the one of Theorem U.44w, except for the overall positive factor $B/\kappa$ in the second-target block. That block still solves (U.44w.1), has zero linear stress, and has the same four massless polarizations. The metric and first-target blocks are unchanged. The proof of the sharp internal gap $4/R_0^2$ therefore applies to each member. These properties concern the unchanged physical angular units and do not identify distinct coefficients by a field rescaling.

*A bounded modification with nonnegative matter energy.* Choose $H$ above with compact support and let $G$ be smooth with compact support and $G(x)=x$ for $|x|\le\epsilon$. In (U.44z.3a) replace $X_2,X_1$ multiplying the two $H$ factors by $G(X_2),G(X_1)$, respectively. Both winding-neighborhood identities and their comparisons still hold. Put $Q(X_1,X_2)=H(X_1)G(X_2)+H(X_2)G(X_1)$ and $D=\max_i\sup |\partial_i Q|<\infty$. Since $Q(0,0)=0$, one has $|Q|\le D(|X_1|+|X_2|)$. For any unit timelike observer let $a_i$ and $b_i$ be the squared norms of the time derivative and the spatial gradients of $N_i$ in the observer's orthonormal frame. Thus $X_i=b_i-a_i$. The stress energy density is $2\sum_i a_i\partial_i U+U$, where the matter Lagrangian is $-U=-[\kappa(X_1+X_2)+(B-\kappa)Q]/2$. It is bounded below by $[\kappa-3|B-\kappa|D]\sum_i(a_i+b_i)/2$. Hence there are distinct coefficients arbitrarily close to $12$ even among smooth actions with nonnegative matter energy for every first jet and every timelike observer. This energy bound supplements the hyperbolic reference neighborhoods.
