 \longrightarrow\mathcal N\cap H^1
$$

is an isomorphism by the specified full spectral gap and elliptic regularity. Its $L^2$ realization has domain $\mathcal N\cap H^2$ and index 2. The analytic implicit-function theorem applied to

$$
P_NF_{1+\delta}(Q+k+h)=0,
\qquad k\in K,\quad h\in\mathcal N\cap H^3              \tag{U.73b.6.10}
$$

gives the unique analytic normal graph $h=h(k,\delta)$ near zero. It satisfies $h(0,\delta)=0$; at $(k,\delta)=(0,0)$ its derivative in $k$ vanishes. Every nearby full critical point lies on this graph.

For $a\in\mathbb R^4$, put

$$
k_a=(0,a\cdot\nabla q),\qquad
u(a,\delta)=Q+k_a+h(k_a,\delta),\qquad
R(a,\delta)=E_{1+\delta}(u(a,\delta)).                    \tag{U.73b.6.11}
$$

This restriction does not discard other angular sectors. To show that it is the full centered problem, consider the involution

$$
\mathcal I(z,w)(x)=(z(-x),-w(-x)).
$$

It preserves the action, $Q$, $K$, and $\mathcal N$; it acts as $-\operatorname{Id}$ on $T$ and $+\operatorname{Id}$ on $U$. It fixes $k_a$. Uniqueness in (U.73b.6.10) therefore forces $u(a,\delta)$ to satisfy $z(-x)=z(x)$ and $w(-x)=-w(x)$. Its Euler vector has the same parity. Thus its entire $T$ projection is zero. The $\mathcal N$ projection is zero by construction. Since $\partial _a h$ is normal,

$$
\partial_{a_i}R(a,\delta)
 =\langle F_{1+\delta}(u(a,\delta)),(0,q_i)\rangle.
$$

It follows that

$$
F_{1+\delta}(u(a,\delta))=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla_a R(a,\delta)=0.   \tag{U.73b.6.12}
$$

Conversely, an arbitrary nearby $H^3$ critical point can be centered uniquely by a small common translation so that

$$
\langle z(\cdot+c)-q,q_i\rangle=0\quad (i=1,\dots,4).
$$

For the finite-dimensional implicit-function theorem, move the translation onto the smooth test functions: $\langle z(\cdot+c),q_i\rangle=\langle z,q_i(\cdot-c)\rangle$. The center derivative at $Q$ is the invertible Gram matrix $NI_4$. Translations are continuous on $H^3$, so the centered point remains in the chart. Its $K$ coordinate belongs to $U$, and uniqueness in (U.73b.6.10) places it in (U.73b.6.11). This proves all-angular local exhaustion without assuming differentiability of the translation action on arbitrary $H^3$ fields.

Spatial rotations act equivariantly on $a$, because $q$ is radial and the projections commute with rotations. Consequently $R(Oa,\delta)=R(a,\delta)$ for $O\in O(4)$. Its analyticity implies

$$
R(a,\delta)=r(s,\delta),\qquad s=|a|^2,                  \tag{U.73b.6.13}
$$

where $r$ is real analytic for $(s,\delta)$ in an open neighborhood of $(0,0)$, including formal negative $s$. One way to see this is to restrict to $a=te_1$: the convergent analytic power series is even in $t$; rotational invariance then identifies its even powers with powers of $s$. Only $s\ge0$ corresponds to fields.

##### V. Exact comparison manifold and evaluated quartic

The decoupled comparison functional $\mathcal D$ has the exact critical manifold

$$
M_b=(z_b,w_b),\qquad
z_b(x)=\frac{q(x+b)+q(x-b)}2,\qquad
w_b(x)=\frac{q(x+b)-q(x-b)}2.                              \tag{U.73b.6.14}
$$

Indeed $z_b+w_b=q(\cdot+b)$ and $z_b-w_b=q(\cdot-b)$ are independent critical points of $S$, so $\mathcal D^{\prime}(M_b)=0$ and $\mathcal D(M_b)=S(q)$ exactly. Its full version also allows a common center; no positivity-only normal restriction is involved.

The parameter $b$ in (U.73b.6.14) is a literal half-separation for the comparison pair. The coordinate $a$ in (U.73b.6.11) is a fixed-kernel projection. They agree to leading order but should not be silently identified beyond that order. Specifically, the $T$ projection of $M_b-Q$ is zero by parity, and its $U$ coefficient is

$$
a_i(b)=N^{-1}\langle w_b,q_i\rangle,
\qquad a(b)=b+O(|b|^3).
$$

The local inverse is $b=b(a)=a+O(|a|^3)$; it is smooth and O(4)-equivariant. All expansions hold in every fixed required Sobolev space because $q$ has the relevant derivatives. Hence

$$
\widehat M_a=M_{b(a)}=Q+k_a+h_D(a),
\qquad h_D(a)\in\mathcal N\cap H^3,
\qquad h_D(a)=O(|a|^2).                                  \tag{U.73b.6.15}
$$

At $\delta=0$, (U.73b.6.3)–(U.73b.6.4) and exact criticality for $\mathcal D$ show

$$
\|F_1(\widehat M_a)\|_{H^1}=O(|a|^3).
$$

A uniform local inverse for the normal equation therefore gives

$$
h(k_a,0)-h_D(a)=O_{H^3}(|a|^3).                           \tag{U.73b.6.16}
$$

More generally, the normal residual from $\delta\mathcal G$ is $O(|\delta||a|)$, so

$$
h(k_a,\delta)-h_D(a)
 =O_{H^3}(|a|^3+|\delta||a|).                             \tag{U.73b.6.17}
$$

These estimates follow, for example, by subtracting the normal equations, writing their difference as an average of normal derivatives, and using that this average is a small operator-norm perturbation of the invertible normal Hessian. This keeps the two negative directions in the inverse.

Let $v=u(a,0)-\widehat M_a$. By (U.73b.6.16), $v=O(|a|^3)$. Since $\mathcal D^{\prime}(\widehat M_a)=0$, Taylor's theorem gives

$$
\mathcal D(\widehat M_a+v)=S(q)+O(|a|^6).
$$

Also $\mathcal P^{\prime}(\widehat M_a)=O(|a|^3)$, so $\mathcal P(\widehat M_a+v)-\mathcal P(\widehat M_a)=O(|a|^6)$. Along (U.73b.6.14),

$$
z_b=q+O_{H^3}(|b|^2),\qquad
w_b=b\cdot\nabla q+O_{H^3}(|b|^3).
$$

The $H^3$ product estimates then give

$$
\mathcal P(M_b)=-2\int q^2(b\cdot\nabla q)^4+O(|b|^6)
              =-2C|b|^4+O(|b|^6).
$$

The last equality follows by rotating the vector $b$ to the first coordinate and using radiality of $q$. Replacing $b$ by $b(a)=a+O(|a|^3)$ changes no quartic coefficient. Therefore

$$
\boxed{R(a,0)=S(q)-2C|a|^4+O(|a|^6),\qquad C>0.}         \tag{U.73b.6.18}
$$

In particular the normal correction cannot cancel the quartic. It begins at cubic order relative to the exact comparison manifold, and changes its energy only at order six or higher. This is the evaluated nonlinear coefficient, not a generic uncomputed resolvent expression.

##### VI. Coupling derivative and complete local critical set

Write $u_0(a)=u(a,0)$. By (U.73b.6.15)–(U.73b.6.16), $u_0(a)=Q+k_a+O(a^2)$, with $z=q+O(a^2)$ and $w=a\cdot \nabla q+O(a^3)$. The latter order also follows from the symmetry $w\to-w$ and uniqueness of the normal graph.

Differentiate the reduced action with respect to $\delta$. The normal equation and $\partial_\delta h\in\mathcal N$ cancel the implicit derivative term, giving the exact envelope identity

$$
\partial_\delta R(a,\delta)=\mathcal G(u(a,\delta)).       \tag{U.73b.6.19}
$$

At $\delta=0$ this yields

$$
\partial_\delta R(a,0)
 =\frac12\int A(q^2)(a\cdot\nabla q)^2+O(|a|^4)
 =\frac J2|a|^2+O(|a|^4).                                \tag{U.73b.6.20}
$$

Because $R(0,\delta)=S(q)$ exactly, analyticity, (U.73b.6.18), and (U.73b.6.20) imply the joint expansion

$$
r(s,\delta)=S(q)
 +\left(\frac J2\delta+O(\delta^2)\right)s
 +\left(-2C+O(\delta)\right)s^2+O(s^3),                 \tag{U.73b.6.21}
$$

with analytic coefficients and uniform local derivative estimates. In particular,

$$
r_s(s,\delta)=\frac J2\delta-4Cs
 +O(\delta^2+|\delta||s|+s^2),\qquad
r_{ss}(0,0)=-4C<0,                                      \tag{U.73b.6.22}
$$

and the complete centered critical equation is

$$
\nabla_aR(a,\delta)=2a\,r_s(|a|^2,\delta)=0.             \tag{U.73b.6.23}
$$

The implicit-function theorem applied to $r_s(s,\delta)=0$ gives exactly one small root

$$
s_*(\delta)=\frac{J}{8C}\delta+O(\delta^2).               \tag{U.73b.6.24}
$$

Its derivative at zero is negative. For sufficiently small $\delta<0$, $s_*(\delta)>0$; for $\delta>0$, $s_*(\delta)<0$, which is not a field radius. At $\delta=0$ the only small nonnegative root is zero. These statements are uniform after choosing one sufficiently small parameter interval and field neighborhood.

It follows that every nearby critical point, up to common translations, is:

1. the base point $Q$, for every small $\delta$;
2. for $\delta<0$, additionally the sphere
   $$
   \{u(\sqrt{s_*(\delta)}\,\omega,\delta):\omega\in S^3\}; \tag{U.73b.6.25}
   $$
3. no additional point for $\delta\ge0$.

At fixed $g=1$, therefore, the four extra operator zeros do not integrate into any nearby nontrivial relative critical family. In fact every sufficiently nearby critical point is a common translate of $Q$, a stronger statement than failure of a chosen parametrized family.

The branch (U.73b.6.25) is $O(4)$-equivariant; its individual solutions have $O(3)$ stabilizer and are not $O(4)$-invariant. The sphere consists of rotations of the separation axis. Its embedding is injective because the $U$ projection recovers $a$ exactly. The physical comparison half-separation satisfies $b=a+O(|a|^3)$; on the branch,

$$
|a|^2\sim|b|^2\sim\frac{(g-1)J}{8C}.
$$

The true fields differ from the comparison pair by $O(|g-1|^{3/2})$ in $H^3$, by (U.73b.6.17). The sign-reflected field $w\to-w$ corresponds to $a\to-a$ and lies on the same spatial rotation sphere.

##### VII. Full operator inertia and branch kernel

We now verify the index and nullity in full $L^2$, including every angular sector. At a nearby smooth solution $u$, its Hessian is $-\Delta I_2$ plus a bounded symmetric multiplication potential. Relative to $H_1(Q)$ the potential is small in $L^\infty$ when $\|u-Q\|_{H^3}+|\delta|$ is small. It tends to $\mu I_2$ at spatial infinity because $H^3(\mathbb R^4)\subset C_0(\mathbb R^4)$ and the nonlinear terms vanish at zero. Consequently the essential spectrum is $[\mu,\infty)$.

The fixed-normal compression

$$
B=P_NH_{1+\delta}(u)|_{\mathcal N}
$$

has domain $\mathcal N\cap H^2$, remains invertible, and has exactly two negative eigenvalues. Domain justification follows by the finite smooth constraints: a weak compressed solution differs from an ordinary elliptic equation by finitely many smooth kernel vectors, yielding $H^2$ regularity. The spectral gap and small bounded potential perturbation preserve invertibility and index. No negative mode is removed.

On the form domain, decompose a vector as $k+n$, with $k\in K$ and $n\in\mathcal N\cap H^1$. Completing the square using $B^{-1}$ gives an invertible form congruence between the full Hessian and

$$
B\ \oplus\ \left(P_KHP_K-P_KHP_NB^{-1}P_NHP_K\right).   \tag{U.73b.6.27}
$$

The finite matrix in parentheses is exactly the Hessian of the full eight-dimensional reduced action

$$
\widetilde R(k,\delta)=E_{1+\delta}(Q+k+h(k,\delta))
$$

at a reduced critical point, obtained by differentiating (U.73b.6.10). Hence negative indices add and operator-kernel dimensions equal the finite Schur nullity, since $B$ has no kernel. All $L^2$ zero vectors are $H^2$ by the operator domain and then $H^3$ by elliptic regularity; the finite-dimensional reduction does not miss rough $L^2$ modes.

At a centered branch point, differentiating its exact common translations supplies four Hessian zero vectors

$$
\partial_{x_j}u=(\partial_{x_j}z,\partial_{x_j}w).
$$

Their $U$ projections vanish by parity: $\partial _j w$ is even and $q_i$ odd. Their $T$ projections span $T$, since the associated Gram matrix tends to $NI_4$ as the branch tends to $Q$. Differentiating the normal equation shows that their $K$ projections are zero vectors of the Schur matrix. It follows that the entire $T$ block and both mixed $T\text{--}U$ blocks vanish. The remaining $U$ block is exactly $D_a^2R$.

By (U.73b.6.13),

$$
D_a^2R=2r_s I_4+4r_{ss}\,a a^T.
$$

On the nonzero branch $r_s=0$, $s=|a|^2>0$, and $r_{ss}=-4C+o(1)<0$. This finite Hessian has one negative eigenvalue $4sr_{ss}$ and precisely three zero eigenvalues tangent to $S^3$. Together with the four translations and (U.73b.6.27),

$$
\boxed{n_-(H_{1+\delta}(u))=3,\qquad
       \dim\ker H_{1+\delta}(u)=7\quad(\delta<0).}         \tag{U.73b.6.28}
$$

The three extra zero vectors are the nonzero rotational orbit tangents, and their independence follows from the rank-three derivative of the sphere's $U$ projection. Combined with translations, they exhaust the full kernel. Each fixed small negative $\delta$ thus has a local Morse–Bott critical manifold $\mathbb R^4\times S^3$; the nonzero spectrum is separated from zero at that fixed parameter. No parameter-uniform positive gap is claimed as $\delta\to0$.

The same Schur argument at $Q$, or the direct crossing calculation of Part III, gives the base indices and nullities:

| Coupling | Base index | Base kernel dimension | Additional nearby family |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| $g<1$ sufficiently close to 1 | 2 | 4 | $\mathbb R^4\times S^3$, index 3, kernel 7 |
| $g=1$ | 2 | 8 | none beyond common translations |
| $g>1$ sufficiently close to 1 | 6 | 4 | none beyond common translations |

This table is local in $g$ and in field space. It does not classify distant critical points or other thresholds.

The coupling, cutoff and scalar-profile hypotheses specify this local source completely. Other thresholds, general transverse matrix sources, boundary/extension domains, derivative-dependent, running or other nonhomogeneous models have their own nonlinear problems.
